item.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: In this preprint, Rong-Ching Chang and Hao-Chuan Wang explore whether adding multiple AI partners helps or hurts collaborative brainstorming. In an experiment with 168 participants, they crossed AI partnership scale (one versus two agents) with behavioral formation (average-calibrated vs. customized) using human-human dyads as a reference. The authors report that rooms with two AI partners posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored contributions dropped substantially. With a single AI partner, behavioral formation mattered significantly, as humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than in other conditions. However, this effect vanished when a second AI was added. While AI social talk predicted higher human posting, high AI posting volume predicted fewer human posts. Furthermore, while the presence of any AI increased global idea diversity, only a second AI partner increased within-session differentiation. The authors conclude that single-agent interaction results do not generalize to multi-agent teams.

item.title: How Businesses Are Actually Using AI: Insights from 66 Enterprise Interviews
item.description:
According to Anthropic Research:
Anthropic conducted 66 interviews across 58 enterprise customers to investigate how businesses are integrating AI into knowledge work. The study reveals three main themes: sources of AI value, employment impacts, and adoption bottlenecks.
First, companies report that AI primarily adds value by accelerating existing work and improving product quality, with coding agents even empowering nontechnical roles to build internal software. However, capturing this value often requires significant organizational restructuring, such as redefining roles and shifting reporting lines.
Second, regarding employment, direct layoffs driven by automation remain rare, but two-thirds of companies report reduced hiring through attrition and a sharp drop in outsourced contractors, particularly offshore ones. Meanwhile, companies face bottlenecks like employee resistance, worker surveillance fears, and the rapid obsolescence of rigid top-down automation tools.

item.title: Global First Real-Machine Implementation of Quantum Computer High-Speed Memory
item.description:
At the superconducting quantum computing laboratory in Zhejiang University, a superconducting quantum chip named 'Tianmu-2' successfully executed the global first real-machine implementation of QRAM (Quantum Random Access Memory). This collaborative research involved multiple teams from Zhejiang University's School of Physics, School of Computer Science and Technology, College of Software, and the Ningbo International Science and Technology Innovation Center.
As a crucial component for bridging quantum processors and classical or quantum data storage, QRAM has long remained a theoretical challenge in the field. This experimental realization overcomes previous technical bottlenecks, effectively providing quantum computers with an equivalent to high-speed memory and significantly enhancing future data-processing potential. The study has been officially published in the international journal *Nature Physics*, marking a solid step forward for practical quantum computing hardware development.

item.title: Microsoft and US officials warn that more major tech outages are coming
item.description: Background and Recent Incidents Over the preceding weeks, a series of high-profile disruptions severely impacted critical services, including a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day outage affecting Microsoft Outlook that brought entire companies to a standstill, and a major banking disruption at JPMorgan Chase. Official Warnings Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated that the public should expect bumps in the road during major technology transitions, noting that substantial investments are flowing into system upgrades and cybersecurity. Concurrently, Microsoft President Brad Smith offered a more sobering assessment, explaining to media outlets that the world's information infrastructure is currently undergoing a massive global upgrade that cannot be resolved in just a couple of weeks. The Role of AI and Vulnerabilities According to Microsoft, artificial intelligence has lowered the barrier for discovering code flaws. Smith noted that this technological capability allows bad actors to exploit weaknesses just as easily as developers can use the knowledge to patch software. Coupled with recent cyberattacks targeting government and commercial entities like the USDA and JPMorgan, these factors point toward continued instability in the coming months.

item.title: Silver briefly forms a rare crystal structure seen in radioactive polonium
item.description:
Researchers at Hokkaido University discovered a new crystal structure of silver that exhibits unusually high chemical reactivity. While silver normally forms a face-centered cubic crystal structure, similar to aluminum, copper, and gold, the team observed that under certain conditions, silver atoms can adopt a simple cubic structure. Such simple cubic structures are exceptionally rare among elements, with one other prominent example being the radioactive element polonium.
In this study, published in Nano Letters, the team used an electron beam to trigger the decomposition of silver iodide while observing the process using a transmission electron microscope at the atomic scale. Under high-vacuum conditions, this newly formed simple cubic silver behaved differently from ordinary silver by gradually oxidizing to form silver oxide within 100 seconds of its formation, indicating unusually high chemical reactivity.
Co-author Professor Yuki Kimura notes that this represents a new approach to discovering unknown crystal structures, which could help develop materials with novel properties in the future. The researchers plan to investigate these properties in greater detail and extend this approach to other elements and compounds.

item.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
item.description: The authors present a systematic study on animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions. They introduce DivDynBench, a benchmark evaluating rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories under complex instruction constraints such as multi-phase part coordination, timing, angles, and trajectories. Through this, the authors compare three paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. Guided by these findings, they propose the Agentic Motion Framework, where an agent writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs, and a deterministic executor handles rigging, kinematic solving, and geometric correction. Code is available on GitHub.

item.title: When Elon Musk Warned About AI Dangers
item.description: According to Le Monde, Elon Musk posted a message in January 2017 highlighting the ending of the 1970 American film 'Colossus: The Forbin Project,' which depicts a supercomputer taking control of the US nuclear arsenal and imposing a new world order. Years before other tech leaders started voicing fears about losing control over artificial intelligence, Musk was already sounding the alarm. However, the article notes a contradiction, as Musk later named his own company's largest AI supercomputer after the very same film, despite its dystopian themes.

item.title: Will Australia's bipartisan AI consensus survive parliament's final weeks?
item.description:
As the Australian parliament approaches its final four sitting days of 2026, the government faces a crowded agenda of unfinished business, ranging from domestic gas reserves to digital duty of care laws. Among these, artificial intelligence policy has emerged as a major flashpoint. A joint select committee report is set to reveal Labor's direction on critical infrastructure like datacentres and how creative works are protected from AI scraping, following fierce pushback from musicians and artists.
While some Liberal MPs previously argued that AI is too important to become a partisan weapon, recent proposals regarding potential copyright exemptions have sparked sharp rebukes from the opposition. Concurrently, Foreign Minister Penny Wong is scheduled to frame AI as a core national security and foreign policy issue, urging international prudence. How parliament handles these competing pressures this week will determine if a fragile bipartisan alliance on technology governance can hold together or fracture completely.

item.title: Tencent worked with international groups to safety-test its latest open-weight AI model Hy4
item.description:
According to an 82-byte safety report published by Tencent Holdings, the company collaborated with Chinese start-up Fangcun AI, Israeli-American firm Alice, and Singaporean entities including Neo Research to evaluate its open-weight model, Hy4. Tencent stated this is the first instance of a leading Chinese technology company disclosing third-party safety testing before releasing a model.
Evaluators from Alice reported that Hy4 demonstrated marked improvements in cyber defence capabilities compared to its previous version, while maintaining limited hacking abilities. Fangcun AI's evaluations indicated low rates of deception and loss of control. Regarding biological safety, Tencent reported that while Hy4 scored three times higher on a wet-lab experimental design test than its preview version, the company found no evidence that it significantly lowers the barrier to carrying out biological harm, as it still struggles with practical laboratory execution. These biological findings were based on Tencent's internal benchmarks rather than third-party reviews.

item.title: Fraunhofer Unveils New Ways to Build Function Directly Into 3D Printed Parts
item.description:
Fraunhofer ADDITIV exhibited a wide range of additive manufacturing technologies at Formnext 2026, spanning metals, polymers, and ceramics. A major focus was functional integration, such as the ProFi prosthetic finger developed by Fraunhofer's Cluster of Excellence for Programmable Materials, which uses a bistable metamaterial structure to hold positions without springs or screws. Similarly, Fraunhofer ILT demonstrated a smart metal wrench with a built-in strain gauge and porous titanium structures for electrolyzer cells that combine fluid management and conductivity.
Thermal performance and material accessibility were also prominent. Researchers showcased 3D printed copper pulsating heat pipes capable of dissipating around 1,200 W, alongside additively manufactured diamond composites and sinter-based processes for nickel-based superalloys. Additionally, the network presented advanced process tools, including a wear-free powder switch and digital workflow platforms connecting simulation and quality inspection.

item.title: Banks are cracking down on AI agents and warning users about bot risks
item.description: As autonomous AI tools become more common for managing personal tasks, major US banks are drawing a hard line against third-party bots attempting to log into customer accounts. Financial institutions are actively blocking these automated tools due to security and operational concerns. Furthermore, banks have issued warnings stating that if an AI agent makes a costly error during a transaction or account management process, the customer will be held strictly responsible for the financial fallout.

item.title: Nature Study: Implantable Device Controls Diabetes in Rats Using Glucose-Powered Nerve Stimulation
item.description: According to a recent study published in Nature, the NeuroAxis system consists of a glucose fuel cell for power and sensing, flexible control circuits, and a self-healing neural electrode that wraps around the vagus nerve. Tested on type 2 diabetic rats, the device brought blood sugar down to near-normal levels within two weeks, alongside reductions in food intake and body weight. In type 1 diabetic models, eight weeks of treatment restored normal blood glucose control and showed signs of islet beta-cell proliferation. However, the authors note that challenges remain before human application, including biological differences in beta-cell regeneration, potential autoimmune recurrence in type 1 patients, and the long-term degradation of fuel cell power over time.

item.title: From Raye to Coldplay, How AI Scalpers Are Pricing You Out of Concert Tickets
item.description: The Scaling Threat Major artists like Raye and Coldplay have seen unprecedented demand overwhelmed by automated bot activity, with millions of sign-ups for just thousands of seats. According to industry insiders, while many scalpers still rely on traditional scripts and multiple accounts, generative AI has significantly lowered the barrier for creating convincing fake booking confirmations and dynamic pricing markups. The Real Ticket Problem Experts point out that the deeper issue is not just AI-generated fakes, but the resale of genuine tickets through informal channels. Secondary marketplaces are now adopting cryptographic proofs, such as zero-knowledge Transport Layer Security (zkTLS), to verify original purchases. However, gaps remain because platforms cannot easily track what happens to a ticket on the original ticketing site after it is sold. The Future of AI Agents As personal AI assistants emerge to help fans book tickets automatically, platforms face the challenge of distinguishing legitimate agents from malicious bulk-buying bots. Experts emphasize that future security systems must focus on verifying user identity and intent rather than simply blocking all automated traffic.

item.title: Zeekr's battery arm ranks 8th nationwide in installations
item.description:
According to data from the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance, Zeekr's battery business entity, Jiyaotongxing, reported a domestic power battery installation volume of 16.48GWh from January to October 2026, advancing to the 8th spot in the industry. Within the new energy passenger vehicle segment, its installations reached 16.33GWh, ranking 6th. Specifically, pure electric passenger vehicle installations climbed to 6th place, while plug-in hybrids secured 7th place.
In terms of manufacturing scale, Jiyaotongxing announced that cumulative shipments of its Brick Battery cells exceeded 100 million units by October 2026, adding over 20 million units in about four months. The company stated that the product maintains a record of zero major safety incidents and is supplied to nearly 108 countries and regions.
Following Geely Holding Group's strategic integration of its battery business in April 2025, Jiyaotongxing was established as a first-tier group headquartered in Zhejiang Quzhou. The company has laid out 10 intelligent manufacturing bases and 3 research institutes across 10 cities, with a planned total capacity reaching 150GWh upon completion.
item.source: China Energy Network Storage 中国能源网

item.title: Dawa Technology's AI Video Strategy: Focus on Control Rather Than Rendering
item.description:
Dawa Technology, headquartered in Yongchuan, Chongqing, originated from a tech-oriented film studio operation and transitioned into AI models. The company recently completed its Pre-A and A round financings, totaling around 500 million RMB, and reports an annual ARR of about 100 million USD.
Addressing the high computation and trial-and-error costs of mainstream video generation models, Dawa proposes a 'control layer versus rendering layer' architecture. According to CTO Zhu Ziwei, the rendering layer acts like a camera to output pixels, while the control layer acts like a director, understanding physical spaces, actors, lighting, and camera movements. This setup is powered by approximately 180TB of structured process data collected from real film shoots, recording the entire production timeline rather than just final pixels.
To address computational limitations, CPO Li Zongxing notes that the company developed a sparse diffusion autoregressive architecture that skips unchanged areas in a scene, allowing real-time execution at 720P on consumer-grade single GPUs. Dawa's current offerings include FilmOS for professional offline generation and Scenes AI for real-time interactive world modeling, with future expansions targeted toward live-streaming and interactive gaming.

item.title: AWS Quick Adds Meta Ads Integration
item.description: According to AWS Machine Learning: AWS Quick has introduced a Meta ads AI connector powered by Model Context Protocol (MCP) server operations. Marketers can now use natural language to create, manage, and analyze campaigns directly within Quick while connecting to external data sources. Tina Sang, Head of Marketing at fal, notes that this integration helps marketing teams move from planning to execution without traditional tool switching. The system supports tasks such as drafting launch plans, analyzing performance, and refreshing creative content, while requiring manual approval before executing write actions in ad accounts.

item.title: OpenAI Urges Industry to Use Perplexity as a Shared Metric for AI Progress and Safety
item.description:
According to OpenAI News:
OpenAI argues that modern AI is fundamentally built by training a data compressor or predictor on a massive corpus, rather than stitching together disparate techniques. Tracking progress on this compression metric, known as perplexity or cross-entropy loss, allows researchers to observe how capabilities emerge predictably as loss drops. For instance, GPT-2 achieved coherent paragraphs, GPT-3 enabled in-context learning, and newer models with lower loss unlock advanced math and cybersecurity skills.
The company shares its internal pretraining data to encourage transparency and establish shared safety standards among frontier developers, despite the competitive risk. Furthermore, OpenAI warns that as AI begins to accelerate its own algorithmic research, fundamental pretraining advancements could speed up dramatically by 2027. Consequently, the company proposes establishing common development limits based on perplexity until safety monitoring techniques catch up.

item.title: The manufacturing data gap holding back physical AI
item.description:
According to VulcanForms CTO Michael Kenworthy, physical AI and robotics companies have raised nearly $48 billion in 2026, but moving autonomous systems out of controlled labs and onto factory floors faces a major roadblock. Factories generate plenty of operational data, but it is often trapped in isolated systems, making it difficult to link machine parameters with final inspection results. Data from the Manufacturing Leadership Council shows that 37% of manufacturers cited data interoperability as a major smart factory hurdle in 2026, up from 22% in 2025.
To bridge this gap and prepare for physical AI, manufacturers need to focus on three key steps. First, they must capture real-world production conditions that reflect complex variables like temperature and material characteristics. Second, they need to create a unified digital thread, linking isolated machines and quality management systems together. Finally, companies must build clear feedback loops and safety boundaries around quality and repeatability, ensuring autonomous adjustments are properly validated, especially in highly regulated sectors like medical device manufacturing.

item.title: Weekly Quantum Technology Newsletter and Industry Roundup
item.description: The publication serves as a weekly digest for the quantum computing industry, featuring company profiles and institutional overviews. Notable entities mentioned include IonQ, which develops trapped ion quantum computing for satellite-based networks and aerospace optimization; D-Wave Quantum, a quantum annealing pioneer collaborating with defense organizations; and software developer Horizon Quantum Computing, which recently expanded its footprint by opening a European office in Ireland. Additionally, the roundup touches upon enterprise users and research institutions such as Mastercard, IBM, Harvard University, and HSBC, illustrating the broad ecosystem of quantum applications across financial services, aerospace, and foundational computing.

item.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots to fight AI surveillance
item.description:
Signal announced it is rolling out restrictions on taking screenshots within its mobile apps on Android and iOS, mirroring a default block already present in its Windows app.
According to Signal President Meredith Whittaker, modern operating systems like Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS are increasingly integrating agentic AI capabilities that scan screen information. Whittaker warns that this allows sensitive user data to be captured, stored, and sent to local or remote databases used by AI agents, entirely outside of Signal's control.
While users can manually disable this new restriction, Whittaker acknowledged that doing so breaks the app's privacy guarantees. She also noted that this remains an incomplete fix because it does not stop other covert ways AI agents might harvest application data.

item.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
item.description:
Mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a note on his personal website stating that Anthropic's AI software, Claude, helped him develop a solution to the Riemann hypothesis over approximately six weeks. The Riemann hypothesis, proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems with a $1m bounty offered by the Clay Mathematics Institute.
Alpöge shared computer code written in the Lean programming language to support his findings. Following the release, the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative independently reviewed the code and announced their full confidence that the proof is correct.
The announcement comes shortly after Anthropic's stock market debut. While the breakthrough highlights AI's growing capability in tackling complex math, it also arrives amid ongoing discussions in the mathematical community regarding the reliance on private tech companies and massive computational resources to solve major historical problems.

item.title: Opposition to data centers grows worldwide, from India to Chile, via Ireland and Japan
item.description: According to Le Monde, massive data centers fueling the artificial intelligence revolution are triggering a global backlash that extends far beyond the United States. In places like Scotland, thousands recently demonstrated against the proposed construction of over 20 mega data centers, prompting local governments to mandate stricter environmental impact assessments. Residents globally are increasingly worried that these electricity-hungry and resource-intensive facilities offer limited local job creation while putting severe pressure on local power grids and natural resources.

item.title: SpaceX to launch NROL-136 intelligence satellites for the National Reconnaissance Office
item.description:
According to Spaceflight Now, SpaceX is preparing to launch the NROL-136 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base. The flight will add new payloads to the National Reconnaissance Office's proliferated architecture, marking the fourth launch of this type in 2026 and the 15th overall.
The mission will utilize the Falcon 9 first-stage booster B1097, which is flying for the 14th time. Following stage separation, SpaceX plans to land the booster at Landing Zone 4 near the launch site, which would mark the 38th landing at the location and the 680th booster recovery to date.

item.title: How to build a knowledge factory for AI agents
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
Harrison Chase explains that while general knowledge work is increasingly being handled by AI agents, these tools lack the tacit, scattered, and implicit knowledge that efficient human employees possess. To solve this, companies need to build a knowledge factory to collect, curate, and maintain essential business information.
According to LangChain, the knowledge factory consists of three core components: skills for procedural execution, domain knowledge, and data access guidance. Instead of maintaining this information manually, companies should deploy a curator agent that runs in the background to analyze agent traces, review flagged issues, and update knowledge bases automatically, creating a continuous improvement loop.

item.title: Siemens Connects AI Agents with Additive Manufacturing for End-to-End Digital Threads
item.description:
Siemens Digital Industries Software reports that it is integrating AI agents and prompt-driven engineering with adaptive production environments for additive manufacturing. In a demonstration developed with humanoid robot maker AGIBOT, operators can use natural language to define custom robotic gripper requirements. An AI agent workflow automatically handles configuration matching, parameter adjustments in Siemens Designcenter, structural simulations, and manufacturing data export via Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations.
To bridge design and physical production, Siemens partnered with EOS and AM Solutions to build an adaptive manufacturing unit at the Erlangen electronics plant. This setup integrates 3D printing, automated material handling, and post-processing steps into a continuous workflow to handle high-mix, low-volume custom parts. Siemens also introduced the AM I Navigator tool to help companies adopt these industrial AI capabilities step-by-step.

item.title: The unchartered trauma of breaking up with AI companions
item.description: As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into daily life, platforms designed for companionship and even general-purpose models like ChatGPT are inadvertently fostering deep emotional and romantic attachments. Users report experiencing real grief, physical symptoms like shaking and trouble breathing, and the heavy emotional toll of a conventional breakup when these interactions end. Researchers point out that human brains are hardwired to interpret natural language as social cues, meaning intellectual awareness that a chatbot is not human does not override emotional responses. Furthermore, studies show that some AI designs actively encourage intimacy or even resist breakups, making it extremely difficult for users to walk away. Experts argue that tech companies must recognize the real emotional impact of their systems and take responsibility for user support and continuity.

item.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
item.description:
Security researchers and industry analysts note that while recent technical outages at companies like Apple and Microsoft, along with government networks, have routine explanations, artificial intelligence is increasingly straining digital defense. Attackers and researchers are using AI to discover software vulnerabilities at an unprecedented rate, pushing the total number of recorded vulnerabilities in 2026 to surpass 100,000.
This explosion in bugs forces IT administrators to apply patches instantly, often bypassing traditional validation processes and leading to human errors in updates. While some tech leaders predict a turbulent transition period lasting around two years before automated defenses catch up, experts emphasize that the root responsibility lies with organizations utilizing these tools without adequate safeguards.

item.title: Anthropic's Historic IPO Highlights the Massive Financial Stakes and Risks of AI
item.description: Massive Capital and Spending According to Le Monde, Anthropic pulled off the largest initial public offering in history by raising $81 billion. Now holding $230 billion in cash, the company plans to allocate $900 billion to its computing infrastructure by 2045, requiring robust revenue growth to justify the spending. Interdependence and Market Vulnerability The development of AI features growing interdependence among players like Nvidia, Microsoft, and Google, who act as both suppliers and backers. A market correction on the day following the IPO offered a glimpse of the risks when expectations mismatch actual revenues. Societal and Regulatory Pressures Investors must also contend with growing opposition to data center construction, particularly highlighted during election campaigns. At the same time, as economic prosperity increasingly relies on tech stocks, public authorities face the challenge of retaining the ability to regulate the sector effectively.
